clue.text: "Jaded? One's time on earth ain't fun right?" (Self-deception from 25 23)

indicators.note: deception is trickery, telling us the quoted words and Self are rearranged by sleight of hand

parts.note: the S of the contraction counts as a letter in this anagram fodder

parts.words: time on earth ain't fun right

explanation.surface: A weary soul grumbles about life being no fun, and the setter tags it as self-deception.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Self-deception' splits: SELF joins the quoted words as fodder and 'deception' is the anagram signal; the 36 letters rearrange into the famous saying. 25 23 is the linked answer naming its author.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying is a well-known aphorism attributed to the American writer named at 25 and 23, so it is a quotation from him.

clue.text: Cut page from examination

indicators.note: from here means taken away from, so the page letter is removed from the longer word

parts.note: an inspection is an examination

explanation.surface: Someone tears a page out of an exam script.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a rare noun for a cutting into something, an incision, so it matches the noun cut.

clue.text: Removes oneself from bearing and the womb

parts.note: E, east, is a compass bearing
the loins are the region of the body associated with procreation, standing loosely for the womb

explanation.surface: An odd medical or obstetric note about withdrawing from bearing a child and the womb.
explanation.definitionFit: This archaic legal verb means to take oneself away or withdraw to a distance, so it fits removes oneself.

clue.text: West has transferred work into eastern hellhole

indicators.note: transferred means the letters have been moved about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as part of the fodder
OP, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: A westerner has moved work to a grim factory in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of WEST and HAS are shuffled by 'transferred' to give SWEATSH, then OP (opus, a work) completes it; 'into' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A factory with appalling conditions, often in Asia, is a classic hellhole for its workers.

clue.text: Look at grain from the Whispering Desert!

indicators.note: whispering means the words are spoken, so we hear rather than see them

parts.note: look at is SEE and grain is SEED, together sounding like the answer

explanation.surface: An exclamation about peering at sand grains in a desert of murmuring dunes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert' looks like a noun for sand but is the verb, to abandon.
explanation.definitionFit: To formally withdraw from a union or alliance is to abandon or desert it.

clue.text: United supporters raising chaos

indicators.note: in a down clue raising lifts the letters so the whole run reads upwards

parts.note: U is a standard abbreviation for United, as in football team names
fans are supporters

explanation.surface: Manchester United's followers are kicking up a chaotic fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raising' turns U plus FANS, UFANS, upwards in the down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Military slang acronym for a situation in total disarray, so a synonym for chaos.

clue.text: European with a romantic disposition? Non, Monsieur!

indicators.note: disposition read as dis-position, a placing of letters in a new arrangement
Non, French for no, says the Monsieur letter is not present

explanation.surface: A Frenchman denies being a romantic European.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Non, Monsieur' removes M from A ROMANTIC, leaving AROANTIC, which 'disposition' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Croatia, a country in southern Europe, is a European.

clue.text: As Homer exclaims: "You cannot finish in the sumo ring!"

parts.note: Homer Simpson's catchphrase exclamation is d'oh

indicators.note: the word You is not allowed its final letter

explanation.surface: Homer Simpson shouts at a wrestler that he can't win in the sumo ring.
explanation.walkthrough: Homer is the cartoon Simpson, not the Greek poet.
explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese word for the raised clay ring in which sumo bouts take place.

clue.text: See 1
On which the unemployed needed drink or warm brew before church

indicators.note: before places the preceding letters ahead of the church abbreviation

parts.note: a jar is a drink, especially of beer

indicators.note: brew means the letters are stirred and mixed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, part of the fodder
taken as written, part of the fodder

explanation.surface: Jobless men needed a drink or a warm brew before attending church.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1936 protest march from Jarrow in north-east England to London by unemployed shipyard workers; 'needed' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous 1936 crusade was a march on which unemployed men walked to London to petition for work.

clue.text: See 1
Drug addict turned over, punished with no company and given new life

indicators.note: turned over means the addict word is flipped to read backwards

parts.note: a user is a drug addict

indicators.note: with no says the company letters are dropped from the word for punished

parts.note: corrected can mean punished, as in correcting a child

explanation.surface: A drug addict, having turned his life around after punishment and leaving the firm, gets a fresh start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned over' gives RESU from USER; 'with no' takes CO out of CORRECTED, leaving RRECTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Being raised from the dead means being restored to life, a new life.

clue.text: What might have been televised on buildings

definitions.meaning: crime-scene re-enactments are shown on television to jog witnesses' memories
edifices rebuilt after damage are reconstructed structures

explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both re-enactments of events, as on crime programmes, and rebuilt structures.

clue.text: Poet against falling in love with Psyche

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, the letter O
V, for versus, means against
the id is part of the psyche in Freudian theory

explanation.surface: A poet writes against falling in love with the mythical Psyche.
explanation.walkthrough: Psyche looks like the mythical maiden loved by Cupid, but it is the Freudian mind, giving ID.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman author of the Metamorphoses was a celebrated poet.

clue.text: See 1
Wildly incited "no smoking", producing lungs like this?

indicators.note: wildly signals the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written, part of the fodder
taken as written, part of the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone has been rabble-rousing for no smoking, pointing to blackened lungs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smoking' completes the definition's picture rather than giving letters: lungs stained by smoking.
explanation.definitionFit: Stained or tainted with tobacco residue describes the lungs of a heavy smoker.

clue.text: Swallows' child heard against mischief-maker; prepare yourself!

indicators.note: heard signals that the letters are to be taken as they sound when spoken

parts.note: titty is a nursery word for the breast from which a child swallows milk
V, for versus, means against
Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin

explanation.surface: Gossip about a young bird is aimed at a troublemaker, followed by a call to get ready.
explanation.walkthrough: Ate, Greek goddess of mischief, is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: To smarten oneself up before going out is to prepare oneself, so it fits as an imperative.

clue.text: Profit from a sincere relationship

indicators.note: relationship hints at the letters being related to one another afresh in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone gains from an honest partnership.
explanation.definitionFit: A rise in value or earnings is a gain, so profit and the answer are synonyms.

clue.text: NASA project failing means panic

indicators.note: failing means the letters collapse and reassemble in another order

explanation.surface: A space mission going wrong causes panic at mission control.
explanation.definitionFit: NASA's Mercury programme was its first project to put an astronaut in orbit.

clue.text: Nasty exposures revealing fault on one's shutter

indicators.note: revealing says the letters are shown within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A photographer's nasty overexposures reveal a fault in the camera shutter.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as photography; the 'shutter' is in fact the eyelid.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflamed swelling on the eyelid is a blemish on the eye's own shutter.

clue.text: But did it knit jerseys?

parts.note: knit means join and jerseys are cattle, so this reads as a bovine adhesive, a brand of rubber glue

explanation.walkthrough: Jerseys are Jersey cows, not knitted pullovers; the answer is a British rubber-solution adhesive brand.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubber-based glue used for sticking paper; its name pairs a cow with gum.

clue.text: Hare was cooked to rest in curries

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters have been stirred together and transformed

explanation.surface: A hare was cooked and left to rest in curries.
explanation.walkthrough: Hare is not the animal but William Hare, the Edinburgh body-snatcher partner of Burke.
explanation.definitionFit: Hare was a nineteenth-century body-snatcher, one who dug up corpses for sale to anatomists.

clue.text: Is raising invoice from the speaking oracle

indicators.note: in a down clue raising lifts the word Is so it reads upwards
from the speaking says the invoice word is taken as it sounds when spoken, not as spelt

parts.note: a bill is an invoice; said aloud it gives the last three letters with a Y

explanation.surface: An oracle is billing clients in person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raising' turns IS to SI; the word for invoice, spoken, supplies the rest, so the whole sounds like SI-BILL.
explanation.definitionFit: A prophetess of the ancient world, such as at Cumae, who uttered oracles.

clue.text: Advice on dodgy affair last thing one needs

parts.note: end and last both mean the final part
it can mean the thing in question

explanation.surface: An agony aunt says to finish a shady fling, the last thing anyone wants to hear.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the blunt counsel to finish a risky romance.

clue.text: See 25
One horse ran out backwards and died; one was very close

indicators.note: out here means outside, so the reversed ran wraps around the others
backwards means ran is read from its end

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
gee-gee, GG, is a child's word for a horse

explanation.surface: One horse ran out and finished backwards before dying, after it had been very close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backwards' reverses RAN to NAR, placed 'out', around IGG. 'very close' means stingy, not near.
explanation.definitionFit: A miser is someone close-fisted, and close here means mean with money.

clue.text: US philosopher deconstructing treble nucleus with Shakespeare

indicators.note: deconstructing means taking the word apart and putting its letters together differently

parts.note: a hub is a centre or nucleus
the Bard is Shakespeare's nickname

explanation.surface: A literary theorist deconstructs a treble core alongside Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: The American writer and Roycroft founder was known for his philosophical essays and aphorisms.
